label: before
limitation: HEADLESS CHROME EMULATION on a desktop host, NOT a physical device. Viewport/dpr/isMobile/hasTouch/reduced-motion emulated; CPU/GPU/thermal/real-touch/mobile-network are NOT. Frame-time and memory are host-relative; before/after compared under identical conditions.

_meta.purpose: Experience-level performance budgets for the redesigned Rustwake game. These are ceilings a player should never feel exceed, NOT a byte-shaving contest. The historical 233000-byte entry ceiling is explicitly NOT a hard constraint here; entryDecodedBytes is a realistic headroom budget, and total transferred bytes are measured as decoded payload (this build ships procedural audio + procedural canvas sprites, so binary media is zero).
_meta.groundedIn: Baseline measured at main f80726970287a9c6da96e0c475b77dc0daccd96b via tests/perf/perf-67.evidence.mjs (vite preview of the production build, headless Chromium, 6x CPU throttle for the low-end pass). See docs/PERF_BUDGETS.md for the full protocol and the device-vs-emulation limitation.
_meta.evaluationNote: The probe compares interaction budgets against the MEDIAN open/tap latency (the budget keys retain the *P95Ms names the probe reads). Frame budgets use P95 of requestAnimationFrame deltas. 'met=null' means not measured (e.g. landscape machine-tap automation does not land) or no budget set; those are reported as unknown, never silently passed.
_meta.deviceLimitation: All numbers are AGENT headless emulation on a fast host with a local preview (no real network, no real low-end GPU/compositor). Emulation is a necessary-but-not-sufficient floor: meeting a budget here does not prove a real mid/low-end phone meets it. Frame time stays at the 60Hz vsync floor (16.8ms) even at 6x CPU throttle on this host, so throttled interaction latency is the sensitive rerender-cost signal.
